previous_assumption: The Product Catalogue's minimal skeleton (id, productCategoryId, manufacturer, name, createdAt on Product; single-level ProductCategory) was treated as a reasonable starting shape, with capacity/spec fields undecided.
correction: After inspecting the legacy schema (116-page phpMyAdmin export) and a representative production data sample (oem_fleet, fleet1, images), the owner locked a richer catalogue design: (1) ProductCategory -> ProductSubcategory -> Product hierarchy, confirmed by real data where every sub_type mapped to exactly one category with zero cross-category leakage across 118 rows. (2) Product gets relational `capacity` (numeric, nullable) + `capacityUnit` (nullable, must be a constrained set not free text -- legacy data showed 'M³' vs 'm^3' as the same unit stored two inconsistent ways). (3) Product gets a `specifications` jsonb column for category-specific technical/transport specs, grouped by real co-occurrence (boomFamily, craneRigging, fluids, transport) rather than ~19 flat nullable columns like legacy's fleet1/oem_fleet tables. (4) Machine gets a new `chassisNumber` (nullable text) field -- legacy evidence: `chassis_number` is populated only in the per-unit fleet1 table, never in the per-model oem_fleet catalogue table, confirming it is a physical-unit identifier. (5) `manufacturer` stays Product-level only; Machine has no manufacturer field of its own -- it is inherited by callers via `machine.productId -> product.manufacturer`. (6) Chassis manufacturer (legacy `chassis`/`chassis_make`) is explicitly deferred -- real data showed one genuine conflicting-value example (same make/model with chassis 'Ashok Leyland' in one unit vs 'MAN' in another), enough to disprove 'always fixed by the model' but not enough to confirm systemic variance from a ~118-row sample, so it is intentionally left off both Product and Machine pending a direct business answer.
